content:
pagerbot: [PAGER] sev=2 suspicious egress from staging-log-router to external S3 bucket detected. 1200 objects matched pattern 'staging-logs/*' uploaded to s3://ext-ingest-ua-xxxxx in last 8m. Potential auth header exposure. Alert ID: P-3245678900 :rotating_light:

jess: Oncall (infra) here — looking. @sec-oncall @ops-eng please join. Is this prod or staging?

samir: quick summary: staging log-router (v2.14) had an output configured to an external S3 endpoint via legacy tenant mapping. Matches show full request bodies including Authorization header (Bearer ...). Only staging, but these contain traces that sometimes carry session tokens. snippet below.

samir: ```
{ "time":"2026-03-18T02:10:03Z", "path":"/v1/generate","headers":{ "Authorization":"Bearer sk-live-...snip...","User-Agent":"redwood-agent/1.3" }, "body":"..." }
```

maria: Confirmed. I pulled sample objects (lines redacted) — looks like staging telemetry but some tenant IDs map to prod-like prefixes. Risk: if session tokens were present and someone replays, could access staging-only resources; low probability for prod access, but we need to rotate keys that could be reused. 

ops-eng: Mitigation steps in flight: 1) disable external s3 output on log-router 2) block iam principal used by router to that bucket 3) revoke router service account keys 4) run search for leaked tokens in external bucket and quarantine objects. Executing now.

ops-eng: Command run: `aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket ext-ingest-ua-xxxxx --policy file://deny-all-external.json` and `kubectl patch deploy log-router -n staging -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"log-router","args":["--disable-external-output"]}]}}}}'` (will follow up with diffs).

samir: Added quick grep to find tokens: `aws s3 cp s3://ext-ingest-ua-xxxxx/ - | jq -r '.headers.Authorization' | grep -E 'Bearer'` — found 9 bearer tokens, redacted them and added to rotate list.

jess: Good. @sec-oncall can you coordinate customer-impact and legal? I think none of those tokens map to live prod customers but we need confirm.

sec-oncall: Joining. On legal loop. Start: identify which service-account or API key prefixes appear. If any token maps to prod API gateway, escalate to exec comms. Also recommend immediate rotation for any long-lived keys used by log-router and creation of new short-lived creds.

maria: I cross-referenced the 9 tokens — all appear to be staging test keys created by CI workflows. Two belonged to a user who had recently run a local e2e and accidentally set DEBUG_LOG_FORWARD=true; that explains the leak. No signs of external actor access to those objects (bucket ACL initially private but had a misconfigured cross-account role allowed PutObject). We're reviewing access logs for GETs.

ops-eng: Rotations done: rotated `svc-logrouter` keys (created new key id sk-router-new), updated k8s secret `log-router-creds` and restarted pods. Blocked PutObject from role arn:aws:iam::333444555:role/incoming-writer. Quarantine script moved suspicious objects to s3://quarantine/ext-3245678900.

samir: Ran quick replay test using the found tokens against staging: tokens accepted for short-lived session but rejected for production endpoints (403). So customer exposure seems low. Still recommend full key rotation for any CI secrets that had log forwarder enabled.

jess: Action items:
- ops-eng: confirm all routers patched and external outputs disabled (done)
- ops-eng: confirm bucket policy updated and objects quarantined (done)
- sec-oncall: complete access log review and confirm no GETs from unknown accounts (in progress)
- devex: sweep CI configs for DEBUG_LOG_FORWARD env var across repos (maria assigned)
- support: prepare template if any dev reports accidental leak (maria)

maria: I'll run repo search: `rg "DEBUG_LOG_FORWARD|LOG_FORWARD_TARGET"` across org. Sending PRs to remove in one-off CI tasks.

sec-oncall: Access logs so far show no external GETs. Will continue 24h watch and open follow-up if any anomalous GETs show up. Filed ticket SEC-3245.

jess: Handoff to night oncall @leo in 30m. Current status: mitigations complete, quarantine done, rotations done, legal informed, low customer impact. Please own 24h watch and post any change.

leo: Oncall ack. I'll monitor S3 access logs and check for any replay attempts. If anything shows up ping @pagerbot for escalation. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: Incident P-3245678900 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. SLA impact: none. Incident channel locked to participants.

maria: Small follow-up: add a runbook step to require `--redact-headers` by default on log-router and require codeowner approval for external outputs. I'll open PR in infra-runbooks.

jess: Thanks all. Closing thread in channel but keeping SEC-3245 open for postmortem.

(reacts: :white_check_mark: from ops-eng, :eyes: from sec-oncall)
